entries.question: What is TigerLegs?
entries.answer: TigerLegs splits a swimrun, a race course or one of your own training sessions, into its swim and run legs. You load a GPX file and get a map and a table with the distance of every swim and run.

entries.question: Why the name 'TigerLegs'?
entries.answer: The "legs" are the swim and run legs of a swimrun course, which is what the tool splits out. The tiger is amphibious and a good swimmer, like a swimrunner, and a nod to Team Groot Rondje Eilanden. It is also a backronym: Terrain Informed Gpx ExtractoR: LEts Go Swimrun!

entries.question: Does my GPX file leave my browser?
entries.answer: No. Your GPX file is analysed in your browser and is not uploaded. Terrain data is off by default; the "Your data" section on this page says what is sent if you switch it on.

entries.question: How does TigerLegs find swims and runs?
entries.answer: It combines several strategies, such as waypoints, speed and terrain, and shows in the Detected by column which one found each segment.

entries.question: Can I install TigerLegs as an app?
entries.answer: Yes. Use the Install app button in the footer when your browser offers it. On an iPhone or iPad, tap Share and choose Add to Home Screen.

entries.question: Where can I find swimrun races?
entries.answer: [Dave's List](https://lowtideboyz.com/swimrun-races) of the Low Tide Boyz is a worldwide directory of swimrun races, with a map and a searchable list.

entries.question: Is it finished?
entries.answer: No. TigerLegs is a beta and some features are prototypes, which the pages say. Testers are welcome.
